review_notes:
I found no repeated proof machinery in this file that the rubric would count, so there are no findings.

I read all six declarations (lines 1–101): `unitBitStep`, `unitBitStep_law`, `flatUnitWalk`, `flatUnitWalk_law`, `uniform_singleton_joint`, `unitJointDraw`, `unitJointDraw_law` and `unitJointDraw_variation`.

The only reasoning that appears twice is in `unitBitStep_law` (lines 27–33) and `unitJointDraw_law` (lines 70–78). Both use the same two-step calc:
- rewrite `mapLaw uniformLaw (fun b => g (f b))` as `mapLaw (mapLaw uniformLaw f) g` with `(mapLaw_comp _ f g).symm`;
- then rewrite with the inner law lemma (`smallBitProposal_law_decidableEq` in one, `flatUnitWalk_law` in the other).

`mapLaw_comp` is in `Transport/RationalMapProducts.lean`. It states `mapLaw (mapLaw p f) g = mapLaw p (fun x => g (f x))`. A shared helper of the form "if `mapLaw p f = q` then `mapLaw p (g ∘ f) = mapLaw q g`" would just restate `mapLaw_comp` followed by a rewrite. The rubric excludes thin wrappers around existing API and short calculations, so I did not report it.

The other proofs each do different work:
- `flatUnitWalk_law` transports along an equivalence and applies `wordWalkLaw_eq`.
- `uniform_singleton_joint` combines `mapLaw_deterministicJoint`, fibre subsingletonness, `pointLaw_eq_uniform` and `dependentJointLaw_uniform`.
- `unitJointDraw_variation` combines `variation_map` with `unitSmallWalk_variation`.

I also searched the sibling ContingencyTables files for the fibre-subsingleton/point-law argument. The only other use of `completionFibre_subsingleton` is in `AllSmallFibres.lean` (line 60), where it supports a different conclusion, so it is not a duplicate of `uniform_singleton_joint` in this file.
